decision.detail: I walk to the station line. The tape is already threaded — I did that an hour ago, set it in the reel head, left the room to let Alma talk. I sit in the chair behind the glass. Dial Pittsburgh. The carrier hums, warms. I don't add a greeting. I say, low, into the mic: "This is for her. It's her mother. She's finished. Play it back when you're ready." I let the line hold for three seconds. I pull the tape from the head, wind it back into the can, set the can in my coat pocket. I stand up. The ballroom lights are still on. I don't look at them. I take my coat off the hook by the door and walk out into February.
decision.intention: Get the recording to the daughter before the night ends and the line goes dead. That's the job. It's done.
decision.words: This is for her. It's her mother. She's finished. Play it back when you're ready.
